Mitochondria play a crucial role in the remodeling of lace plant leaves during programmed cell death (PCD). During PCD, lace plants undergo a series of complex changes that involve the coordinated activity of various organelles. Mitochondria are involved in this process as they release their contents into the cytosol, where they can be taken up by other cells or recycled.

Studies have shown that mitochondrial dynamics are altered during PCD in lace plants, suggesting that mitochondria may be playing a critical role in the development of developmental PCD. Additionally, research has demonstrated that mitochondrial movement on transvacuolar strands to form a ring structure surrounding the nucleus is also involved in developmental PCD.

This process is thought to be essential for the degradation of cellular components and the establishment of a new cell wall, which are necessary for the plant's ability to survive and regenerate after PCD. Therefore, mitochondria appear to play a critical role in regulating programmed cell death in lace plants.

Overall, our findings suggest that mitochondria are indeed playing an important role in the remodeling of lace plant leaves during developmental programmed cell death.
